title: A Recipe for Disaster in Taiwan
gist: Teaser (paywalled after intro) by Rebecca Lissner and Mira Rapp-Hooper arguing the risk of a Taiwan crisis is growing, contrasting Biden's explicit pledge to defend Taiwan with Trump's May description of the island as 'a very good negotiating chip' with Beijing.

themes.theme: Shifting US Taiwan signaling raises crisis risk

insights.claim: Rebecca Lissner and Mira Rapp-Hooper argue that the risk of a crisis over Taiwan is growing.
insights.speaker: Rebecca Lissner
insights.so_what: Elevated Taiwan tail risk matters for semiconductor supply chains and Asia risk premia.
insights.quote: Why the Risk of a Crisis Is Growing

insights.claim: Joe Biden publicly confirmed his administration would defend Taiwan if attacked by China, a departure from the US policy of strategic ambiguity.
insights.speaker: Rebecca Lissner
insights.so_what: Shows US Taiwan policy has swung between administrations, reducing predictability.
insights.quote: his administration would defend Taiwan if the island were attacked by China

insights.claim: In May 2026, Donald Trump described Taiwan in a television interview as 'a very good negotiating chip' in dealings with Beijing and noted the island was close to China but far from the United States.
insights.speaker: Rebecca Lissner
insights.so_what: Signals possible US willingness to trade Taiwan-related concessions in US-China deals; watch for weakened deterrence and Beijing testing.

insights.claim: The authors imply the swing from Biden's explicit commitment to Trump's transactional framing is a recipe for disaster because it muddies deterrence signals to Beijing.
insights.speaker: Rebecca Lissner
insights.so_what: Ambiguous signaling can invite miscalculation — monitor PLA drills and cross-Strait incidents.
